A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OT-CPCC and Fast FlowTree work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite formatting changes and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic timing and approximation experiments, image classification and retrieval results, and hierarchy analyses in Section 4 and Appendices G-H.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds quantitative hierarchy-sensitivity results and real-data training-runtime measurements in Appendices H and K.

M1.justification: The CPCC objective, distribution-based class distances, augmented label tree and FastFT greedy matching procedure remain unchanged, including Algorithms 1-3. The expanded gradient explanation clarifies the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CIFAR10, CIFAR100, INAT, four BREEDS settings, and synthetic Gaussian and mixture distributions. The added sensitivity and runtime measurements reuse existing dataset and task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds Bures-CPCC as an evaluated runtime comparator against l2-CPCC and EMD-CPCC on CIFAR100 in Table 22. v1 already discussed the Gaussian Wasserstein formula mathematically but did not evaluate this comparator. Existing comparison groups are retained.

E3.justification: v2 adds CPCC and classification measurements to the existing tree-depth and edge-weight studies. Appendix K introduces per-epoch timing on CIFAR10 and INAT and per-batch timing on CIFAR100; CIFAR10 timing uses batch size 128. These are added evaluation protocols, while the original benchmark settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Tables 13-14 quantitatively extend the existing hierarchy-depth and edge-weight heatmaps in Figures 10-11, testing effects on hierarchy preservation and classification. Appendix K adds practical runtime and scalability analyses. The earlier ablations and supplementary analyses remain.

E5.justification: The benchmark tables retain means and standard deviations over three seeds, and synthetic timing retains ten-repeat averaging. The new runtime tables also use three seeds. No increased replication, new significance test or changed uncertainty-estimation procedure is reported.

E6.justification: The main benchmark scores and matched detailed tables remain unchanged. v2 adds hierarchy-sensitivity scores and runtime results: Table 21 reports INAT FastFT at 132.01 seconds per epoch versus EMD at 234.68; Table 22 reports CIFAR100 Bures at 33.77 seconds per batch versus EMD at 1.94. These are newly reported results, not performance improvements between versions.

T1.justification: v2 corrects the marginal-vector dimensions in Equation 3 and revises complexity accounting in Table 1, including centroid computation for l2 and Sinkhorn's per-pair dependence on dimension and iterations. Appendix I supplies derivations. The Gaussian proposition, FastFT theorem and substantive existing proofs are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same central claims: generalizing l2-CPCC with optimal transport, providing linear-time FastFT, and improving hierarchical representations. Added evidence and code-access information do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations that approximate hierarchy structures can preserve classification performance, exaggerated edge weights make hierarchy embedding harder, and covariance-based Wasserstein computation is unsuitable for the tested high-dimensional setting. Appendix I also explains practical timing differences through vectorization.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a code-repository address and explicitly documents full-CIFAR100 evaluation without the source-target split, batch sizes for the hierarchy analyses, and runtime measurement setups. The existing hardware and training-hyperparameter descriptions are retained; the additional disclosures do not establish that earlier experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: New Appendix B distinguishes OT-CPCC's distribution-based representations from one-vector-per-label embedding methods, adding references including Weston et al., Sun et al., Liu et al. and extreme-classification work. This is a focused positioning extension; Section 5 and the relationship to Zeng et al. remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose and section order are retained. v2 adds a proof sketch and explanatory appendix sections, makes local wording edits, updates publication and acknowledgment text, and relocates the former Appendix G.4 comparison to I.1.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 13-14 and 21-22, adjusts diagram layout, and redistributes retained figures and tables within the ICLR format. For example, Figure 3 moves from page 6 to page 5. Existing empirical plots and heatmaps retain their content.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's synthetic timings and visual hierarchy ablations, v2 adds practical training-runtime evidence and quantitative sensitivity results, improves complexity accounting, and provides code-access information. These strengthen support and reproducibility incrementally. The broad runtime-superiority wording remains stronger than the small CIFAR10 differences and reported variability warrant, but this does not outweigh the additions.
